<!-- Snapshot of ONE line of the Velostream repo's CLAUDE.md (its "Gating a PR" bullet), kept here because that repo is private and absent from CI. tests/test_gate_routing.sh reads it only when there is no Velostream checkout beside this one; where there is, it reads the real file and also fails if this line has drifted from it. Update it by copying the line verbatim. -->
- **Gating a PR**: run **`velo-pr-gate <pr> <scope-file>`** (from the [`velo-agents`](https://github.com/velostreamai/velo-agents) repo, installed at `~/.agents/bin/`). It reads which gates the diff needs and dispatches each to the model that has earned it — **`code-review` → Codex**, **`check-code` → the free OpenRouter tier** (the default: `--check-code-by free`, $0, dispatched by the script itself so the leg runs without a manual step; recorded and declared **advisory**, Codex stays the gating leg), or **a read-only Sonnet agent** you launch from the `check-code-agent-prompt.md` the script writes (opt-in, `--check-code-by sonnet`, for non-trivial PRs; `velo-gate-post` and `velo-gate` declare the substitution on the comment and the label from the `check-code.by` marker the script records), **`check-code` → opus at `--effort high`** as a dispatched leg only via `--check-code-by opus` / `VELO_CHECK_CODE=opus` (that leg has never produced a report — it times out), **`check-code` → DeepSeek / GLM on OpenRouter** via `--check-code-by deepseek|glm` (no Claude tokens; recorded and declared **advisory** — Codex stays the gating leg), **`check-spec` → velo-local** (planned for any `[#N]`-titled PR that touches `src/`, as well as for a closing-keyword issue with acceptance bars), plus a non-blocking **`second-opinion`** code review on velo-local (leads to verify, never a gate; `--wait` does not wait for it and `velo-gate-run` kills it after a grace once Codex is done; skip with `VELO_SECOND_OPINION=0`). **A planned gate leg that did not run is never posted as a report and never counted as a pass.** `velo-gate-post` refuses a body that says the leg was "NOT RUN"/skipped, and `velo-gate --pass` refuses until every planned leg (code-review, check-code, check-spec) has a report at head. Under minimal burn only parts of the gate may run — but the skip is the user's call, per PR, recorded as `velo-gate-finish <pr> <sha> --pass --waive <gate>='<reason>' --approved-by '<who>'`; the free legs (check-code on the free tier, check-spec and second-opinion on velo-local) always run. Hand-picking the model per PR is the same class of violation as hand-rolling a dispatch: the routing drifted twice in one session, once sending a review to a worker whose report came back `MERGE-READY` while missing a HIGH and asserting a false fact. The script refuses without a scope file (a gate briefed only on a diff reports dimensions, not findings), computes the review's diff range from the last recorded `gate: <name> @ <sha>` so a re-review scopes to the delta, and **refuses an empty range** — reviewing no diff returns a vacuous approve. It launches Codex itself, but only once the brief's `## ATTACK` section is filled — it refuses while that is a placeholder, which keeps the expensive gate a conscious act with a real brief. **`velo-gate-run <pr> <scope-file>`** runs a whole round in one call — plan, brief (`--brief-only`, which dispatches nothing), the brief's ATTACK filled from the scope file's own `## ATTACK` section (a scope without one is refused), `--exec --wait`, then Codex's final message written to `~/.agents/state/gate/<pr>/codex-verdict.md`; launch it with `run_in_background: true`. Once the reports are curated, **`velo-gate-finish <pr> <sha> --pass|--block <check-code-report> <code-review-report>`** posts each stamped with the sha the gates ran against and then records the verdict — idempotent, transient gh failures retried, and a report that did not land stops it before the label is set (`--code-review <file>` alone for a PR with no check-code leg). Always invoke with `--wait`, launched via a Bash tool call with `run_in_background: true` — a PreToolUse hook (`~/.agents/hooks/require-wait.sh`) denies the call otherwise, so a finished gate can no longer go unnoticed. To see where several PRs stand, sweep with **`velo-gate-sweep <pr> [...]`** instead of reading each gate's files (`codex-verdict.md` / `review.log` / `code.log` / `gh pr checks`) one by one — it prints head vs gated sha (with `STALE` when they differ, `STALE?` when the gated sha could not be read), CI (`ci=ERROR` when the read itself failed — never `ci=none` for a failure), gate-running, and the verdicts, ≤30 lines per PR; every read distinguishes absent (`(no gate yet)`) from unreadable (`ERROR(unreadable …)`).
